_doc: Wording for what a villager says about an event, by the speaker's own relation to it (REPAIR_AUDIT_DIALOGUE_CRIME_GUARDS steps S1 and A4-A6; read by game/scripts/ui/dialogue_voice.gd). Presentation only. {victim}/{Victim}: the victim as the speaker names them (kin words below, else the name); {them}: her or him. A list is chosen from by Dialogue._pick (by villager and day, no random numbers); a list keyed by speaker role uses 'default' for any other role.

kin._doc: How the speaker names a relative, by the relative's relation to the speaker and sex; a 'child' entry is how a child says it. {name}: the relative's first name.

witness._doc: S1: the opening line of a villager who knows the listener harmed someone. crime: killing | assault; how: saw (witnessed it) | heard (told, or learned as family); stance: confront | afraid | guarded (DialogueVoice.stance).

child: You killed {victim}! I saw you! I saw you do it!
I saw you kill {victim}! I'll tell everyone!
default: You killed {victim}! I saw you do it!
I saw what you did to {victim}. I saw it with my own eyes, murderer.

child: Don't hurt me! I saw you kill {victim}!
Go away! You killed {victim}, I saw you!
default: Stay back! I saw you kill {victim}. Please, leave me be.
I saw you kill {victim}. Don't come any closer.

guarded: I saw you kill {victim}. I have nothing to say to you.
I was there. I saw you kill {victim}. Go.

confront: They say you killed {victim}. Is it true?
I heard you killed {victim}. Tell me it isn't so.

child: They say you killed {victim}. Please don't hurt me.
Did you kill {victim}? They say you did. Go away!
default: I've heard what they say you did to {victim}. Please, I want no trouble.
They say you killed {victim}. Keep away from me.

guarded: I've heard what happened to {victim}, and what people say you did. Leave me be.
People say you killed {victim}. I'll keep my distance.

child: I saw you hurt {victim}! That's wicked!
default: I saw you attack {victim}. Keep away from us.
You struck {victim}. I saw it, and I won't forget it.

child: I saw you hit {victim}. Go away!
default: I saw you go for {victim}. Please, just leave me alone.
I saw what you did to {victim}. Don't come near me.

guarded: I saw you attack {victim}. We've nothing to talk about.
I saw you strike {victim}. Go about your business.

confront: I heard you attacked {victim}. Is that true?
They say you went for {victim}. Did you?
afraid: They say you attacked {victim}. Please, leave me be.
I heard what you did to {victim}. Keep your distance.
guarded: I've heard about you and {victim}. I'll keep out of your way.
People say you struck {victim}. Leave me be.

witness_brush._doc: S1: the line a busy villager calls out who knows the listener harmed someone, by stance.
confront: Keep away from us! I know what you did!
guarded: I know what you did. Go.

home_death._doc: S1: home()'s line for a household death the speaker remembers. listener: slain by the listener; slain: by someone else ({killer}); starvation; old_age; other ({cause}). slain_unknown: killed, and the speaker does not know by whom (A5: a household learns of the death, not the killer).
listener: We lost {victim}. You know why: you killed {them}.
We lost {victim}, and it was your hand that did it.

talk._doc: A4 (the perspective renderer, REPAIR_AUDIT D4): how a villager tells an event they know, from their own place in it. A clause per event type; {A} the actor as the subject, {A2} a second actor, {V} the victim, {B} the beneficiaries, {Vs} and {Bs} their possessives, {As} the actor's; each is said from the speaker's side: the listener 'you'/'your', the speaker 'I'/'me'/'my', their household 'we'/'us'/'our' (a household is named 'our family' the first time), a relative as family name them ('Mum', 'my daughter Rose'), anyone else by name, an unknown person 'someone'. A type may give clauses by the subject's person (i, we, you; 'default' for anyone else) where the verb changes. frames: how the clause is framed by how the speaker knows it: saw (witnessed), part (took part: the victim, the beneficiary, their household), told ({T}: who told them), rumour (further along). A list is chosen from by Dialogue._pick (by villager and day; no random numbers). Presentation only. A5 news types: {place} the parcel or building as the village names it, {price}/{rent} coins, {thing} the item's name, {G} who gave (household_word aside, 'givers'); a type in household_types is said with the household as its subject ('our family', 'we', 'the Lamberts'); death is worded by its kind (slain, starvation, old_age; never by whom). gift.you_to_ours: a gift from the listener to the speaker or their own people, which the speaker knows of (seen or told): thanks.

gift.you_to_ours: {B} was so happy when you brought {item}. Thank you

hoard_in_famine.default: {A} hoarded food while people went hungry

land_bought.default: {A} bought {place} from the manor for {price} coins

land_leased.default: {A} took {place} on lease from the manor, at {rent} coins a week

no_tool.default: {A} has no {thing} and cannot get one
no_tool.i: I have no {thing} and cannot get one
no_tool.you: you have no {thing} and cannot get one

merge._doc: A6 (REPAIR_AUDIT D3, D5): related events told as one, by rule, in the order given; each rule joins events of its types (the first type first: that is the order they happened) that share what `same` lists (hh: the household; place: the parcel; giver: who gave; victim: the victim) within `days` days. line: by the first event's subject (we, you, i, default); {c1} the first event's clause, {C2} the second's capitalised, {P} the first subject's pronoun (We, You, I, They, He, She) and {have} (have, has), {times} how many when a rule counts (count: true). The joined line is framed by how the speaker knows the first event. Nothing is dropped: every event's own facts (price, place, people) are in its clause. Read by EventTalk (the grouping) and DialogueVoice (the words).

line.default: {c1}. {P} {have} put up a fence there already
{G} has had to feed {B} {times} times this week

history._doc: GM-01 (R4): a family's history as a villager tells it, from a historical record they know (EventTalk.history): who gave (giver: 'you', 'your grandfather', 'my great-grandfather' or a full name), to whom (receiver: 'me', 'my grandmother', or a full name), what ('40 coins'), and what became of the house. {recognise} opens it when the listener is of the giver's line. One line per state; the speaker picks among the options.
recognise: You're one of the {family} family, aren't you?
ours: {Giver} gave {receiver} {what} toward our house when the money ran short. We've lived in it ever since.
{Giver} helped {receiver} build our house: {what} toward it, when there was not enough. It's still ours.
yours: {Giver} gave {receiver} {what} toward that house. It's yours now.
sold: {Giver} gave {receiver} {what} toward a house. It isn't ours any more: {owner} {has} it now.
{Giver} helped {receiver} build a house with {what}. It passed out of the family; {owner} {has} it now.
destroyed: {Giver} gave {receiver} {what} toward a house. It stands no more, but we remember.
{Giver} helped {receiver} build a house with {what}. The house is gone now.
unfinished: {Giver} gave {receiver} {what} toward a house that was never finished.

said._doc: A6 (D5): what a villager says once they have already told this listener something (NPC.talked, by the listener's player reference). again_witness: the opening of a witness who has already said it today, by stance. again_news: an event of their own family's grief or the listener's harm already told, said again at most once a day. nothing_new: no news they have not told this listener.

confront: I've said what I have to say to you.
I know what you did. Go.
guarded: I have nothing more to say to you.

again_news: I've told you what I know.
nothing_new: Nothing new since we last spoke.
Nothing more than I told you.
